Serial hold by the skills seat: this repo's `guard-main-checkout.sh` and `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` are in flight under PR #7749 (the structural linked-worktree test, awaiting approval), so a second PR on the same two files waits.

Blocked-by: #7259

The objectstack half (#15971) is dispatched now; its PR body will list the exact sentences changed so this twin mirrors them mechanically once PR #7749 lands. `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked` for the wait.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Triage note — evidence carried over from **#8287**, closed today as a duplicate of this card. ⛔ Grade and labels untouched: this is `domain:skills`, and `SKILL.md:380` leaves skills-lane findings with that seat rather than the whole-repo round. Posting the facts, ⛔ not re-grading.

**1 · Two of this card's four sites are already done.** PR #7749 (resync, head `92af28038`) ported objectstack#15987's replacement wording into `guard-main-checkout.sh` at **both** of its message sites — lines 86 and 119 in this card's enumeration — along with the ported self-test rows (`says` / `lacks`) that pin the new text. So the remaining surface here is:

| guard | site(s) in this card | state after #7749 |
|---|---|---|
| `guard-main-checkout.sh` | 86, 119 | ✅ done |
| `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` | 552 (**both** refusals, measured) | ⛔ still `re-run with OS_ALLOW_MAIN_EDITS=1` |
| `guard-shared-stash.sh` | 206 | ⛔ unchanged |
| `guard-tree-enum.sh` | 321 | ⛔ unchanged |

**2 · The residual state is not a smaller version of the original — it is a different, worse one.** This card was filed against four guards agreeing on an instruction that cannot work. What #7749 leaves is two **sibling guards for the same escape hatch** giving an operator **opposite** instructions, and the one still advertising the dead remedy is the Bash guard — the one reached when an agent writes through a shell rather than through `Edit`/`Write`. ⚠️ A visible contradiction between two guards is a stronger invitation to route around them than a uniform wrong instruction was, which is the harm this card's own body names.

**3 · Two gate facts, so the remaining work is not assumed to be watched.** `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` is **not** in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json`, and `guard-main-checkout-bash.selftest.sh` asserts **verdicts only, never message text**. ⇒ nothing mechanical will notice the divergence, and nothing will notice if it is fixed and later regresses. That is the case for the per-hook `re-run with` assertion this card's Deliverable already asks for — it is the part that keeps the fix from being re-lost, not a nicety.

**4 · One open question #8287 raised and this seat did not answer**: whether objectstack's Bash guard carries the same stale line. If it does, the pair lands as one flight in the shape #7749 / objectstack#15924 used. ⛔ Not measured here — objectstack's tree was not read for this. Worth checking before scoping, not worth assuming.

⚠️ This card is `pm:blocked` with no blocker named in its labels' history that this seat can see. If the blocker was #7749 (the resync that would have collided on `guard-main-checkout.sh`), that PR's landing clears it and the card can move to `pm:queue` — ⛔ but that is the skills seat's call, not this one's, so the label is left as it stands.
